question.text: The minimum investment required from each investor in an AIF under SEBI regulations is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, an AIF shall not accept a capital commitment of less than INR 1 crore from an investor. Employees or directors of the AIF or its Manager have a lower minimum of INR 25 lakh, and Accredited Investors may be exempt from this minimum subject to the prescribed conditions. The Trap: INR 25 lakh (Option B) applies only to employees/directors, not to general investors. The INR 1 crore threshold is the standard minimum and acts as a suitability filter to restrict AIFs to sophisticated investors. Note: Category I and II AIF schemes are close-ended with a minimum three-year tenure, so the INR 1 crore floor and the long lock-in together act as a suitability filter for sophisticated investors.
